title: Self-diagnosing cross-regime integrator orchestration
novelty_claim: A gravity simulator can be novel without inventing a new integrator if it adds a controller layer that detects unsafe regimes, escalates solver or precision choices automatically, and emits human-readable intervention logs for plausibly wrong but visually convincing runs.
closest_prior_art: The real overlap risk is the mature REBOUND-style integrator ecosystem named in results/swarm/gap_map.md, especially WHFast, IAS15, MERCURIUS, and TRACE; the local watchlist is mostly off-domain keyword noise rather than direct overlap.
differentiation: The contribution is not raw solver speed or another standalone integrator. It is an orchestration and trust layer: explicit regime detection, safe cross-regime handoff, and user-facing diagnostics that explain when the simulation should no longer be treated as reliable.
easiest_falsifier: A closed feature audit finds an existing gravity simulator that already combines automatic regime detection, safe solver switching, explanation or audit logs, and reproducible replay across mixed long-horizon and close-encounter workloads.
evidence_plan: Precondition: regenerate or supply the missing swarm scout artifacts results/swarm/hypothesis_bridge.md, results/swarm/hypothesis_negative_space.md, and results/swarm/falsifier.md so the novelty case does not rest on gap_map alone.
Build a tight feature matrix against the REBOUND family and comparable gravity simulators before any implementation work.
Use exactly three canonical stress cases: long-horizon secular orbit, close encounter or scattering, and high-eccentricity regime shift.
Kill the hypothesis if the orchestration layer does not surface a materially earlier or more useful unsafe-state warning than fixed-step and hybrid baselines.
budget_envelope: Small-to-medium: one narrow prior-art correction pass, one closed-set feature audit, and three canonical stress cases; no broad literature refresh.

title: Commodity-hardware deterministic replay with fidelity envelopes
novelty_claim: The research wedge is a gravity simulator that runs on commodity hardware while guaranteeing replayable trajectories under a declared determinism contract and publishing explicit fidelity envelopes instead of presenting every interactive run as equally trustworthy.
closest_prior_art: The closest relevant overlap named in results/swarm/gap_map.md is REBOUND browser mode plus SimulationArchive and related reproducibility tooling; the gap is the lack of a clear deterministic replay story for creator-facing or browser-adjacent gravity sims.
differentiation: The differentiator is not simply running in a browser or on a GPU. It is the combination of decoupled render and physics timing, cross-runtime replay guarantees, and published error or fidelity bounds for accessible hardware targets.
easiest_falsifier: An existing browser or commodity-hardware gravity simulator already provides seed-stable replay under declared runtime conditions with an explicit fidelity envelope, or the required determinism assumptions are so restrictive that the commodity-hardware claim collapses.
evidence_plan: Precondition: regenerate or supply the missing swarm scout artifacts results/swarm/hypothesis_bridge.md, results/swarm/hypothesis_negative_space.md, and results/swarm/falsifier.md.
Create a closed feature audit against browser demos, REBOUND browser mode, and reproducibility tooling already cited in the repo artifacts.
Define the determinism contract before implementation: same seed, initial conditions, time-step policy, and physics mode must replay identically within an explicit tolerance budget.
Kill the hypothesis if replay guarantees only survive under narrow hardware or runtime constraints that no longer qualify as commodity hardware.
budget_envelope: Small-to-medium: one narrow reproducibility audit, one determinism contract, and a limited runtime-matrix design; no wide search.

title: Event-aware differentiable gravity simulation
novelty_claim: A gravity simulator can still be genuinely novel if it supports differentiable workflows across non-smooth events such as close encounters, captures, merges, collisions, or solver switches while making gradient trust and fallback behavior explicit.
closest_prior_art: The overlap named in results/swarm/gap_map.md is emerging differentiable N-body or orbit-inference tooling plus close-encounter solver families such as TRACE; the open question is whether those systems already cover non-smooth events with robust gradient semantics.
differentiation: The contribution is not smooth differentiable orbit fitting. It is explicit event handling for gradients: declared safe regions, declared invalid regions, and fallback behavior when events or solver changes break naive differentiation.
easiest_falsifier: Existing differentiable gravity or orbit-inference systems already handle close encounters, merges, and solver switches with robust gradients or explicit fallback semantics, or the remaining problem reduces to ordinary smooth-force differentiation.
evidence_plan: Precondition: regenerate or supply the missing swarm scout artifacts results/swarm/hypothesis_bridge.md, results/swarm/hypothesis_negative_space.md, and results/swarm/falsifier.md.
Run a closed overlap audit against differentiable N-body and orbit-inference systems before any design or implementation work.
Use exactly three event classes for validation design: close encounter, merge or collision, and solver-switch boundary.
Kill the hypothesis if the proposed gradient-trust layer does not add a materially clearer or safer contract than existing differentiable tooling.
budget_envelope: Medium-risk but still narrow: one targeted overlap audit, one event-class matrix, and no implementation until the missing scout artifacts are restored.
